solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Official place left out? Concentrate again

indicators.note: left is read as the abbreviation for left, and out says that letter is dropped from the place word

blocks.note: short for referee, the match official
locus is Latin for place, used in English

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an official site has been omitted and urges everyone to focus once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Locus is the Latin for place, common in English, especially in maths and law.
explanation.definitionFit: To refocus is to bring attention or a lens back to sharpness a second time.

clue.text: Olympic city’s diplomacy is what may keep the peace

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics

explanation.surface: A host city's diplomatic manner is credited with keeping order at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a 1714 British law read out to disperse unruly crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the old statute ordered rioters to disband, so it was meant to preserve public order.

clue.text: River flowing through German university city

definitions.text: River flowing through German university city

blocks.clueFragment: River flowing through German university city
blocks.note: surface reading: a waterway passing a German college town
setter's reading: the river through Hamburg, Dresden and Wittenberg, all with universities

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a plain description: the great river of eastern Germany passes several university cities, Wittenberg and Dresden among them.
explanation.definitionFit: This major central European waterway runs past Dresden, Wittenberg and Hamburg, each home to a university.

clue.text: Rows of conifers seen around one US city

indicators.note: the trees are pictured standing on both sides of the number, wrapping it

blocks.note: banks are tiers or rows, as of oars or switches

explanation.surface: Lines of evergreen trees surround a lone American town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rows looks like quarrels or lines of seats; banks here are tiers, as in a bank of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairbanks is a city in central Alaska, the state's second largest urban area after Anchorage.

clue.text: Boorish and surly colt ready to take offence

blocks.note: c is the racing-form abbreviation for colt
huffy means touchy, quick to sulk

explanation.surface: A young horse is rude, sullen and quick to bristle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives chuffy as a dialect word meaning churlish, rude in manner and sullen.

clue.text: No script circulated, party stuffed? Could be my fault

definitions.text: No script circulated, party stuffed? Could be my fault

indicators.note: circulated suggests the letters going round and coming back mixed up
something stuffed has filling pushed inside it, so a word goes into the jumble

explanation.surface: A political aide, after an unscripted mess and a party in trouble, admits the blame may be theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a press handler whose party is in a fix with no script out might have to take the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor manages a party's public messaging, and so carries responsibility when that messaging collapses.

clue.text: England’s opener in shock review at Headingley?

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for shock

explanation.surface: An English opening batsman is caught out by a surprising decision review in a Test at Headingley.
explanation.walkthrough: Headingley is a cricket ground in Leeds; in cricket an appeal asks the umpire to give a batsman out. E goes inside APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer's appeal is a request for the umpire to review the play and rule the batter out.

clue.text: Who contrived the end of Maggie?

definitions.text: Who contrived the end of Maggie?

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
the end of points to the closing letter of the name that follows

explanation.surface: A question asking who plotted the downfall of Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Maggie is Margaret Thatcher; Geoffrey Howe's 1990 resignation speech set off the leadership challenge that ended her premiership, so the whole clue is the answer's description.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Howe's resignation speech triggered the challenge that toppled Thatcher as prime minister.

clue.text: Fruit a great deal lacking in pith

indicators.note: pith is the core, so the word loses its central letter

explanation.surface: Plenty of fruit lacks the spongy white layer under the peel.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter A of HEAPS is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heps, a variant spelling of hips, are the fleshy red fruits of the wild rose.

clue.text: Macaque lacking colour tied up miles away

indicators.note: the abbreviation for miles goes away from the word for tied
in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a boat moored is tied up

explanation.surface: A pale monkey is tethered a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: Tied up looks like one phrase, but up is the reversal signal on its own; tied alone is the moored boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The wanderoo is the lion-tailed macaque of southern India, a monkey of that genus.

clue.text: Links in headlands with no end of green

indicators.note: with no says a letter is taken away from the headlands word
end of picks the final letter of the colour word

explanation.surface: A golf course on coastal promontories has run out of putting surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Links looks like a golf course, especially beside green; it is S-shaped chain links. N is removed from the front of NESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esses are S-shaped pieces, such as the S-shaped links of a collar or chain.

clue.text: Used to be behind a lot of fit Amerinds

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut
behind places the first-named words after the second

explanation.surface: Someone who was once in great shape is now lagging behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit reads as healthy and the clue makes it an object of behind; it is the adjective chipper, cheerful and well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chippewa, also called Ojibwe, are a Native American people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Rule out regular course getting a passing mention

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for rule is removed from the course word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rule
an orbit is a repeated path round a body

explanation.surface: A ruling bars a usual route, which then earns only a brief reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A passing mention' looks like a casual remark; passing here means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary notice records someone's death, so it is literally a mention of a passing.

clue.text: Boycott pleased he’s excited the country

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of those two words are agitated

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire cricketer, is delighted and thrilled by a Test-playing nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott looks like the cricketer's name, but it is the verb meaning refuse to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a South Asian nation that became independent from Pakistan in 1971.

clue.text: Spurs dispensing with Walker finally to get winning scores

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so a letter is dropped from the spurs word
finally picks out the closing letter of the name before it

blocks.note: a rippon or ripon is a spur, from the Yorkshire town once famed for making them

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, nicknamed Spurs, drop their player Walker and then win.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs looks like the football club; it is the riding gear. R comes off the front of RIPPONS.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo an ippon is the full point that wins the bout outright.

clue.text: Reject a search with only one recipe that’s not kosher

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the words that follow are turned round
with only one says the doubled letter is kept just once

blocks.note: to ferret is to search about
R, from Latin recipe, heads a prescription

explanation.surface: A cook throws out a hunt through a cookbook with only one recipe that breaks dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: One R is dropped from FERRET, A goes in front, and the lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Terefa, also trefa, is Hebrew for food forbidden under Jewish dietary rules.

clue.text: Singer hasn’t many fans

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are scattered and re-laid

explanation.surface: A performer complains of a small following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' reads as admirers; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shantyman leads the sea shanties sailors sang while working, so he is a vocalist.

clue.text: Father’s unchanged after returning

indicators.note: the word reads the same when turned back, so it is unaltered by going in the other direction

blocks.note: describes a word that reads identically either way

explanation.surface: Dad comes back home just the same as when he left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is followed only by a description of the answer's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba is the Aramaic word for father, used in the New Testament as a name for God.

clue.text: Fruit loaf? Take dough first

indicators.note: first says the money word goes in front of the head word

blocks.note: both are slang for the head

explanation.surface: A baker considers fruit bread, starting with the dough.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf and dough both look like baking; each is slang, for head and for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadnut is the starchy edible fruit of a tropical tree related to the breadfruit.

clue.text: Lord’s close matches producing lots of runs?

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the Ashes are the England-Australia Test series

explanation.surface: Tight Test games at Lord's, the London cricket ground, yield heavy scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground and the Ashes the England-Australia series, so runs looks like cricket scoring; it means sprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashes are short fast runs, so several of them are a number of sprints.

clue.text: Putting game out of one’s head, hide in retreat

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: out of one's head means mad
to hide is to thrash, as is to flog

explanation.surface: A fugitive, out of their mind, hides away in a sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide looks like conceal; it is the verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy golf is the British name for miniature golf, played only with a putter round novelty obstacles.

clue.text: Keeping oneself in order, must try cane!

indicators.note: put in order means rearranged, so the letters following are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: A stern instruction that self-discipline requires a taste of the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping oneself in order' reads as the whole definition; 'in order' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Encraty is self-control, the virtue of restraining one's own appetites and passions.

clue.text: Charlie’s girl working after depression is a dish

indicators.note: after places the hollow word in front of the rest

blocks.note: a col is a dip in a mountain ridge
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A man's girlfriend gets back to work after low spirits and turns out to be attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish looks like slang for an attractive person; it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Colcannon is an Irish dish of mashed potato mixed with cabbage or kale.

clue.text: Newspaper’s written about one sort of seasoning

indicators.note: written about means set down around, so the paper word wraps the number

blocks.note: a paper is a party's or group's organ

explanation.surface: A paper's food column covers one type of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ORGAN after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Origan is an old name for wild marjoram, the herb also called oregano.

clue.text: Rose, head dropping is one moving slowly

indicators.note: with its head dropping, the flower word loses its very first letter

blocks.note: a rambler is a climbing rose

explanation.surface: A rose with a drooping bloom takes its time.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose could be the past tense of rise; it is the climbing plant. Its first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambler walks at a leisurely, easy pace, so is someone going without hurry.

clue.text: Salmon before sandwiches indeed reflected Indian food

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards
to sandwich is to hold between, so the first words enclose the agreement word

blocks.note: par or parr is a young salmon
a is the abbreviation for ante, before

explanation.surface: Fish is served before a sandwich course and admired in the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: A parr is a young salmon before it goes to sea; the abbreviation a for ante, meaning before, is a Chambers convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is a fritter of vegetables or meat in spiced gram-flour batter, a South Asian snack.

clue.text: Kick pedal one put to some purpose

blocks.note: to use is to employ for an end

explanation.surface: A cyclist pushes the pedal for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers lists this spelling as a Scots word for a kick; the everyday sense of stopping briefly is not the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots the word means to kick or strike with the foot, a dialect sense recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Advanced part of telecommunications code is a stinker

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced
Toc was the old signallers' word for the letter T

explanation.surface: An early stretch of telecoms coding turns out to be dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Before the NATO alphabet, British army signallers said Toc for T, as in Toc H.
explanation.definitionFit: The atoc is a South American skunk, an animal famous for its foul-smelling spray.

clue.text: Term for the stomach turning up is “belly”

indicators.note: a term is an end, so the term of the next word is its last letter
in a down entry, turning up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the maw is the stomach or gullet

explanation.surface: A dictionary note says that the word for one's tummy is belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like word; it is end. Wame is Scots for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wame is the Scots and northern English word for the belly or womb.

clue.text: Old governor I’m not sure is one to toe the line

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor

explanation.surface: A former ruler hesitates over whether someone will conform.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who obeys follows orders and rules, which is what toeing the line means.

clue.text: Wanting power, first tipped to be leader abroad?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so P for power is missing from the next word
tipped over, a down entry is turned upside down so its letters reverse

explanation.surface: A powerless favourite is tipped to become the ruler of another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped to be' sounds like a forecast; tipped is the reversal. The question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or commander in some Muslim countries, so a foreign head of state.

clue.text: Information department put out guidance for treatment and it’s free

indicators.note: put out means ejected, so those letters leave the next word
something sent for treatment is worked over, so its letters are reworked

blocks.note: I for information plus D for department

explanation.surface: A public information office issues medical advice at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Free looks like costing nothing; it is a verb meaning release.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncage an animal is to release it from captivity, setting it at liberty.

clue.text: Muslim community imam must back? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only a part of the words is used
back means the letters are read from right to left

explanation.surface: Must a congregation back its prayer leader, though not wholeheartedly?
explanation.definitionFit: The umma is the worldwide community of Muslim believers bound by their shared faith.

clue.text: Revised US rates including room for old teacher

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are reworked
including means holding inside, so the reworked letters take in the room abbreviation

blocks.note: rm is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: New American charges cover accommodation for a former schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A surmaster was a deputy headmaster in certain English schools, St Paul's among them.

clue.text: Go off German poet? Easy for another poet!

indicators.note: off means removed, so the word go is taken off the poet's name

explanation.surface: A German poet is told to leave, while another poet finds it simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing GO from GOETHE leaves the answer; the definition's 'another poet' is Spenser, who used the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethe is a Spenserian spelling of eath, an archaic word meaning simple or not difficult.

clue.text: Praise as before all round concerning colony of birds

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so the praise word wraps the next one

blocks.note: herry is an old Spenserian verb for praise

explanation.surface: Old-style praise is lavished on a nesting colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' is Mephisto's signal for an archaic word, here one used by Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronry is a breeding site where many herons nest together, usually in tall trees.
